chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), regarding the eggs of the sandgrouse (quail-like bird), the expiation is like that of the ostrich eggs.

key_terms.بَيْضِ الْقَطَاةِ: Eggs of the sandgrouse (a type of bird)
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Expiation or compensation for a religious violation

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim eating sandgrouse eggs?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi‘ (peace be upon him) to clarify the specific *kaffarah* for a pilgrim consuming sandgrouse eggs, equating it to the penalty for ostrich eggs. This comparison highlights the juristic principle of treating distinct avian species similarly in terms of ritual impurity and expiation when their culinary or biological classifications align in the context of *ihram*. The narration underscores the precision of Imami fiqh in addressing specific dietary prohibitions during the Hajj pilgrimage.
